# Quality rules and the checks that enforce them

Every defect the owner found becomes a **rule** and, where possible, an **automated check**.
Before every merge into `claude/foundation`:

1. Run `node tools/audit/mergeGate.mjs` (or `node tools/merge.mjs <branch>`, docs/WORKFLOW.md). All rows must PASS (exit 0).
2. Run the browser gates it lists, including the **visual tour** (docs/TOUR.md): `debug/tour.html` on the branch, then
   `node tools/tour/compare.mjs foundation <run>`. Look at every flagged view and explain it in the merge message.
3. After the merge, the branch's tour run becomes the new `foundation` baseline (the old one is kept as
   `foundation-pre-<branch>`).

This page is GENERATED (`node tools/docs/rulesIndex.mjs`) from one file per rule, `docs/rules/<slug>.md`; the `meta`
gate row fails when it is stale. To add a rule: a new `docs/rules/<slug>.md` (`added:` date, `check:`, **Rule.** and
**Why.** paragraphs; no number: rules 1-48 keep theirs for history, new ones are named by slug), plus its gate row
`tools/audit/gate.d/<name>.mjs` (node, offline) or `tools/audit/gate.d/browser/<name>.mjs` (needs the viewer), then
regenerate this page. See docs/WORKFLOW.md.

| [alloc-rate](rules/alloc-rate.md) |  (provisional) | Code on the per-frame path (updaters, the instance gathers, culls, render hooks) and the per-tile / per-landmark builds that run while the player plays allocate nothing per item. That means index loops, never `for (const [a, b] of list)` or `const [x, z] = ring[i]` in a hot loop; reused scratch objects, arrays and answer objects; no closure, `subarray` view or small array per item; flat parallel lists in place of `[a, b, c]` tuples; numbers or flat typed lists as Map / Set keys, never template strings. A function every ground query calls (one in `world.decks`, a surface or height lookup) starts with a box test, so a point anywhere else in the city costs four compares. A hot double loop does not live inside a long function, a generator, or a closure's captured variables: there every double is a new heap number (an unoptimised function, a context slot). It goes into a small module function with its state in a typed array or an object of fields. three's own allocating helpers (computeBoundingBox / Sphere: getX per read) are wrapped or replaced from our side by a loop that gives the same numbers; vendor/ and three stay untouched. A GPU readback (`readRenderTargetPixelsAsync`: a staging buffer and a typed array each call in three r187) is never made every frame: it is paced, or it lives at a listed one-off call site. A result that depends on what is loaded (a partial average with a tap in a tile not loaded yet) is cached until the loaded set changes. It is never recomputed on every call. Before you say a change is allocation-neutral, measure it with `node tools/perf/allocSample.mjs --mode falcon\|police`: its "ours" table charges each sample to our nearest function, with builtins as `our frame > builtin` and three as `[lib] fn < our frame`. Each fix stays behind its `?x=old` switch, with a row in viewer/features.js. Every merge that touches viewer/ or models/ passes the `allocbudget` row: the sampled JS KB a frame of a short falcon flight and a short police drive stays under tools/perf/allocBudget.json (the measured value + 25 %). A real increase is measured again (`node tools/perf/allocBudget.mjs --measure`), and the budget is raised in the same merge, with its reason written here. | The owner's #1 complaint is lag in the police game. Hence the `allocbudget` row (claude/allocrate2). Flying the falcon allocated 3-4.5 GB of short-lived garbage a minute (FALCON_STUTTER round 2), and the major GCs paused 50-100 ms. A typed-array probe found ~90 % of it was JS objects, not arrays. On 2026-11-22 the first allocation-sampling profile (CDP HeapProfiler with the objects collected by minor and major GCs kept; 40 s flights and drives) put about 1.8 MB of JS a frame on the falcon flight. It named these sources on our side, in KB a frame of the falcon flight: - the trams' rail lift, 150 (trackProfile.js liftOf): a tram outside the loaded ring recomputed a partial average, 17 road taps each returning a new object, every frame, because only a full average was cached; - the garden clear-ring test, ~170 (main.js inClear): every ring was tested whole, with array destructuring per vertex; the same disease was in cityFuel's ring test; - the instance gather, ~165 (instanceStream.js gather / copy): for-of and destructuring inside a generator, plus a subarray view per copied run, nearly every frame while moving, because TRIGGER is 2 m; - the landmark car blockers, ~60 (heroColliders.js): a closure per triangle; - the parked fleet, ~20-50 on the police drive (carFleet.js): a `[batch, car, fade]` array per drawn car per frame; - the exposure meter: a readback every 4th frame. | `allocrate` (tools/audit/allocRateCheck.mjs: the garbage-free paths give the old results (round 2: the villa deck, the blockers' rect merge and walk, surfaceLayers, the heap drop's bounds bit for bit, the fleet's placeCars car by car, the villa tree clear), the partial rail lift kept until the loaded tiles change, the readbacks listed, the switches' rows) + `allocbudget` (tools/perf/allocBudget.mjs: a 25 s falcon flight and a 25 s police drive under the sampler, the sampled JS KB a frame under tools/perf/allocBudget.json) + browser row `allocrate` (debug/falconStutter.js allocMB a minute and the largest GC drop; tools/perf/allocSample.mjs KB a frame) |
| [asset-compression](rules/asset-compression.md) |  (provisional) | Every file the live site sends goes out compressed or is already compressed inside. A compressible type (glb, bin, json, u16, ... `BR_EXT` in tools/asset_hashes.mjs) gets a brotli-11 sibling `<file>.br` from the Vercel build (`node tools/asset_hashes.mjs`, env VERCEL=1; content-addressed cache in `.vercel/cache/assetbr`), listed in `/asset_hashes.json` `br` (path -> raw size) and served with `Content-Encoding: br` (vercel.json; tools/tour/serve.mjs does the same). The service worker fetches the sibling and answers with it only if the decoded bytes have the listed size AND the content hash; anything else (the CDN re-encoding it, no sibling, an old copy) answers the plain file and turns the siblings off until the next page load. Its answers for a listed file carry ETag `"h-<content hash>"` and it answers that file's HEAD from the list, so the tile cache's dependency tags stay consistent. Without the service worker (the first requests of a first visit, `?sw=0`, a local server with no list) the plain files are served exactly as before; `?assetbr=old` turns the siblings, the `?v=` handling and the hash tags off. A new data type must be added to `BR_EXT` or shown incompressible (the gate measures it); a KTX2 must be zstd- or BasisLZ-supercompressed, because Vercel sends `image/ktx2` raw. Never ship a file as `<name>.glb` with compressed bytes inside or a `Content-Encoding` on a plain path: a client or CDN that does not decode it breaks. | docs/PERF_RESEARCH_2026-11.md idea 1 assumed Vercel sent glb / bin / u16 raw. Measured on the live site on 2026-11-22 (node, `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`), that was wrong: Vercel already brotli-compresses them on the fly, at about brotli level 3 (E4 buildings.bin 461,136 B against brotli-3's 461,141 B). Only image/ktx2, the images and the wav files go out raw, and ours are already compressed inside. So the doc's build-time gzip plus `DecompressionStream` plan would have saved about 2 % (gzip-9 is no better than Vercel's brotli-3). What does save bytes is the level: brotli 11 is 24-37 % smaller than what Vercel sends. On the cold boot's own request list (397 files in the first 33 s) that is 144.6 -> 132.8 MB at today's coverage. With the tiles' `?v=` files also going through the worker, the local 50 Mbit/s stand-in measured 118.3 -> 96.0-96.5 MB before the cover. The bytes are only trusted after a hash check in the worker, because a pre-compressed file sent with a hand-set `Content-Encoding` cannot be tested on a protected preview, and the CDN could legally re-encode or strip it: the check makes the worst case one wasted file, never a broken model (claude/assetgz). | `assetgz` (tools/audit/assetGzCheck.mjs: every listed type is a brotli-sibling type or proven incompressible, every KTX2 supercompressed, the vercel.json header + build wiring, a sample's siblings decode to the source byte for byte and are >= 25 % under what Vercel sends, sw.js in node takes a sibling only when its decoded bytes match the content hash) |
| [hide-ids-full-uri](rules/hide-ids-full-uri.md) |  (provisional) | A scripted model's placement lists the UrbIS solids and buildings it replaces (hides_solids / hides_bu_ids) as the FULL UrbIS URIs the tiles carry (https://databrussels.be/id/buildingsolid/<n>, .../building/<n>), and every id matches a solid of the tile the model stands on; a list that matches nothing is an error, never a silent no-op. | The villa's first placement gave the bare numbers (543176, 1588559): tileData.js hideBuildings compares the ids as given, nothing matched, and the old house's hip roof and chimneys stood through the middle of the villa's flat roof (first browser look, 2026-11-22). Nothing checked that a hide list hid anything. | `villa` (tools/audit/villaCheck.mjs: the villa's hide lists match a solid of tile H9) |
| [interior-stream-paced](rules/interior-stream-paced.md) |  (provisional) | An interior cell that streams in builds its pipelines ONE material at a time, a few frames apart, while it is hidden (never all at once), shows its meshes one per frame behind glass that starts opaque, and animates only the glass's opacity (its transparency state is fixed: no pipeline switch); no light, no shadow caster, no envmap is made for it. Its stream-in is measured with the dynamic resolution fixed (?dynres=0), so the city's own scale adaptation and the machine's load are not taken for the cell's cost. | The villa's round-2 stream-in compiled its 16 materials in one compile call: 16 async pipelines and their shader modules in a burst stalled the GPU process (50 ms frames with no main-thread long task, reproduced with the dynamic resolution fixed); with the dynamic resolution on, the run also mixed in its scale changes on a GPU that the preflight showed 100 % busy before the test. | browser row `villa` (0 frames over 33 ms in 3 stream-in runs, ?dynres=0, on a GREEN preflight) + `villa` (the budgets) |
| [service-vehicle-passage](rules/service-vehicle-passage.md) |  (provisional) | A service vehicle (an ambulance or fire engine on a run, a bus, a bin lorry) always has a physical way. (1) Parking: every parked car leaves SERVICE_CLEAR = 3.0 m of carriageway across from its inner flank, to the far edge of its own carriageway (a kerb, a median, a tram reservation, an unsurveyed cell) or to the next parked car across (Brussels practice for the fire brigade; the widest service vehicle, a bus 2.55 m, + 2 x 0.2 m). Where both kerbs cannot keep it, the way's one-kerb side keeps its cars (the OSM parking tags, else the side with fewer driveways / stops, as the width rule picks it) and the other's go; where one side cannot, none (viewer/streets/parkPlace.js serviceClear; ?parkservice=old). No parked car within MOUTH_CLEAR = 5 m of a junction turn's end, a lane mouth (Belgian highway code art. 24; viewer/traffic/trafficGraph.js; ?parkmouth=old). (2) Routing: every lane has its clear width (trafficGraph.js laneClearWidths: the open width across the lane point over the drawn carriageway and past the parked boxes, a narrowing held over two stations 3 m apart); the router gives a service vehicle a lane under its width + 0.4 m only when there is no other way on (trafficSim.js clearWeight, x 0.001; ?clearroute=old). (3) The sim's courtesy, as drivers give it: a car keeping right for a run whose shifted body would run into a parked car ahead keeps its lane instead (?yieldkeep=old); at a narrow stretch (the two directions' lanes within 2.3 m) a car does not enter while a run comes the other way, and the run squeezes past oncoming cars that stand there when its body clears each by 0.15 m, at 2.5 m/s at most (?runsqueeze=old). (4) A car eased out past a parked car moves back toward its lane line only when the corridor ahead there is no worse than where it is, within ROOM_AHEAD (trafficSim.js makeRoom; ?easeback=old): the moves in are judged like the moves out. (5) The trafmix gate gives the sim the parked cars main.js draws: a tile's cars under a loaded neighbour's core lane are dropped (viewer/traffic/borderPark.js laneHits). | The PARKING job's two trafmix.stuckOld places (?streetlanes=old) were not what their name said. Dieweg E6 (seed 7, -962, 798): one kerb parked, 5.5 m clear; the oncoming cars kept right for the ambulance, pushed their bodies toward a parked car ahead, stopped for it for good; the ambulance waited at the narrow stretch for them to leave it: a deadlock in the yield, not the width. Rue Engeland D7 (seed 23, -1102, 1066): a bus queued behind a car waiting at a parked car 1.9 m from a lane's end, inside the posed turn's sweep, at a dual carriageway's merged junction whose mouths lie 13 m out from the node (the width rule keeps 12 m off a way's end only); the car was also under a neighbour's core lane, which the city never draws but the gate kept as an obstacle. With those fixed, the reshuffled seeds exposed two more run deadlocks of the same kind (an ambulance at a 100 m narrow street, 4.75 m clear, D6 (-1151, 837), cars entering it toward the run while the queue there stood at a red light) and a lane-mouth gridlock at D6 (-1254, 805) with parked cars inside the mouth. The kerb-to-kerb width alone also cannot see a street split by a tram reservation (Rue Engeland: 21 m kerb to kerb, 3.5-5 m each way), so the clearance is measured from each car across its own carriageway. | `servicepass` (tools/audit/servicePassAudit.mjs: every parked car leaves 3 m, all tiles, + the census), `trafparkshove` (tools/trafParkSimTest.mjs on another parked set: 60 shoved cars, seed 11) and `trafmix` (tools/audit/trafmixGate.mjs: "service vehicles fit their lanes": no run / bus / bin lorry into a lane narrower than itself where a wider way went on; "service vehicles stuck": seeds 7 / 11 / 23, register trafmix.stuck / trafmix.stuckOld) |
| [signal-demand](rules/signal-demand.md) |  (provisional) | No traffic-light approach carries more than 0.9 of its green-time capacity at the peak. The capacity is 1,800 veh/h per lane (the base saturation flow of the Highway Capacity Manual, HCM 6th ed. ch. 19: 1,900 pc/h/ln base, about 1,800 for an urban lane with heavy vehicles and turns) times the green share of the signal cycle (22 s green of 54 s). The spawned density on such a lane is capped accordingly: k <= 0.9 x 1,800 x g / C / v at its speed limit (viewer/traffic/trafficSim.js laneDensity). The data hold no traffic counts of Uccle at 8 h. Signal junctions closer than 150 m along a road share the one city-wide cycle (viewer/traffic/signals.js CYCLE). The through movement between them is on the same phase at both: a green wave with offset 0, the link run inside one green. Per-junction offsets would need per-junction light heads (the drawn lights use two city-wide phases). Baseline at the street4 merge: 3 through movements on different phases (n140271967 <-> n2448080511 both ways at D7, n30151287 -> n254921174); claude/signals1 took them to 0: the phase comes from the road at the junction (rule signal-phase-road, signals.js signalPhases, one table for the posts AND the traffic); no offset other than 0 is possible with the two city-wide phases (see that rule). | At the peak, the 8 h density on the Ch. d'Alsemberg arterials (24-26 cars / km / lane) was more than a 22 s green passes. Queues grew without bound and locked the close D6 / D7 junctions (trafmix: service vehicles standing for good). | `trafmix` (tools/audit/trafmixGate.mjs: "signal approaches under capacity"; "close signal pairs coordinated": off-phase pairs <= PHASE_MAX, a ratchet, 3 at claude/street4 -> 0 at claude/signals1) and `sigphase` (all tiles, rule signal-phase-road) |
| [signal-phase-road](rules/signal-phase-road.md) |  (provisional) | A signal approach takes its phase from the road it belongs to at its junction, never from the raw direction of a post. One table, `signalPhases(roads)` (viewer/traffic/signals.js), built from the tile's roads.json alone, is read by the traffic graph (viewer/traffic/trafficGraph.js: every signal approach, `phaseAt(node, road)`) AND the drawn posts (viewer/streets/signalPlace.js signalSites: the signal node the post's traffic meets along its road, `ahead` + `phaseAt`), so a head shows red exactly when the cars facing it stop. The table groups each signal node's arms into two axes (the most opposite pair of arms and the arms within 45 deg of it; the others), and colours the nodes (a parity union-find) so that a road linking two signal nodes under 150 m apart, through plain 2-arm nodes, is on one phase at both ends: close pairs run as one system, a green wave of offset 0. A junction whose signals are mapped on its approaches (traffic_signals up to 40 m out on two or more arms, none on the junction node) is grouped the same way and linked to them. Each cluster's orientation is the one agreeing most with the old direction rule (B north-south). An odd ring of links cannot be coloured with two phases: its least link (a one-way side street before a two-way road, then the longer link) is left off phase; 1 such ring in the city (E1 Avenue Coghen / Rue Vanderkindere / Ch. d'Alsemberg), a ceiling that never goes up. No green-wave offset other than 0: the lights have two city-wide phases (A, and B = A + half the 54 s cycle); a two-way road gets a green wave both ways only with an offset of 0 or half a cycle (the offset one way is minus the other's), and the links are under 150 m (<= 18 s at 30 km/h, inside the 22 s green), so 0 serves both directions; another offset would need per-junction head, walk and sim timings. | The phase of a post was phaseOfDir of the nearest road segment of its OSM point (B where \|uz\| > \|ux\|), and every approach took the phase of the post it passes. Where a road bends, or runs near 45 deg, two posts of the same road a few metres apart fell on different sides of the rule: the through movement between close junctions was on two phases (trafmix: n140271967 <-> n2448080511 on Rue du Wagon both ways, n30151287 -> n254921174 on Avenue Brugmann / De Fre; 5 of 54 through movements city-wide), so a car released by the first green met the second red inside the first junction, and a queue at the second stood in the first one's turn. At the D7 Ch. d'Alsemberg junction n150588281 the signals are mapped on the approaches only, each was phased on its own, and crossing streams arrived together at the uncontrolled centre (the yield inside a turn, gap trafmix.stuck cell -1350, 1250). | `sigphase` (tools/audit/sigphaseCheck.mjs, all tiles: close links on one phase, links across tile borders, posts show their approach's phase, crossing arms apart, the old rule fails) and `trafmix` (tools/audit/trafmixGate.mjs: "close signal pairs coordinated", off-phase pairs <= PHASE_MAX 0; "posts and lanes on one phase") |
| [tile-cache](rules/tile-cache.md) |  (provisional) | A gate row builds a tile with the tile worker's code in node only through the gate's tile cache (`tools/gate/tileBuild.mjs` `tileData(entry, base)` in place of `buildTileData`, or `tools/gate/tileCache.mjs` `cached()` for another builder). The cache key is content: the import closure of the builder's code (for the worker, the closure of `viewer/tileWorker.js`, the same files `tools/build_worker.mjs` bundles and `tools/merge.mjs` hashes), the canonical build options, the node version, the browser stand-ins the build sees, and every file the build read, folder it listed and existence it tested, recorded while it built and re-hashed at every lookup. Only plain data is stored (no function, no class instance); what a row needs of the live objects (keepNet's `net`, `hm`) is kept as plain data by name and any other part throws. A build an input of which changed while it ran is not stored. Writes are a temp file + rename; the cache is capped (`TILE_CACHE_MB`, 4096) with LRU eviction; `--no-tile-cache` (mergeGate or a row) or `TILE_CACHE=0` turns it off, `TILE_CACHE=verify` builds every hit fresh too and throws on a difference. | A full gate built the same 120 tiles ~4.8 times (the road stage ~579 builds) in rows that each rebuilt them from data/tiles; a `--changed` gate on a tile-core change took ~35 min. A cache that can serve a tile built from older code or data would pass a gate that the fresh build fails, so correctness comes first: content keys rather than timestamps or branch names, the inputs recorded rather than listed by hand, the code key checked against esbuild's own list of the bundle's inputs, a byte-for-byte comparison of cached against fresh builds in every gate that touches the tile core, and the tracer (tools/gate/trace.mjs) still seeing every input on a hit so the memo and `--changed` keep the true dependencies (claude/tilecache, docs/SPEED_PLAN.md job 8). | `tilecache` (tools/audit/tileCacheCheck.mjs: the mechanism on a synthetic build + I6 / H6 / E9 cached == fresh, byte for byte); `meta` (tools/audit/metaGate.mjs: the cache's code key covers every input of the worker bundle) |
| [tree-crowns-clear-villa](rules/tree-crowns-clear-villa.md) |  (provisional) | A tree the city keeps near a scripted building never reaches into it: a tree is cleared when its trunk stands where the building is built OR when its crown disc (the tree's `crown` radius, 3 m when the data has none) comes within 0.5 m of the building's footprint (for the villa: the house with its overhangs and entrance, the terrace and pergola, viewer/villa/villaPlot.js CROWN_UW); a trunk-only test is not enough. | The villa's first round cleared the trees by trunk position only (BUILT_RINGS): a 9.5 m tree 2.7 m north of the living wing kept its 2.5 m crown, and its leaves hung inside the double-height living room and through the north wall (the coordinator's review of after_day_living.jpg, 2026-11-22). | `villa` (tools/audit/villaCheck.mjs: no kept tree crown within 0.5 m of the house / the terrace) |
| [vehicles-touch-ground](rules/vehicles-touch-ground.md) |  (provisional) | A parked vehicle a scripted place adds stands on its four wheels: the body is set from the drawn surface sampled under the four wheel contact points (their mean, pitched and rolled to their slopes: viewer/villa/villaPlace.js), never from one height at its centre, and every wheel is within 5 cm of the paving; under a roof where the sun's shadow map never reaches, it gets a soft contact shadow. | The round-2 saloon in the villa's garage was set from one height at its centre and had no shadow under the garage's ceiling: it read as floating (the coordinator's review of after_day_garage.jpg, 2026-11-22). | `villa` (tools/audit/villaCheck.mjs: every placed vehicle's wheels within 5 cm of the paving) |
| [villa-budgets](rules/villa-budgets.md) |  (provisional) | The villa on Av. du Prince d'Orange (viewer/villa/) stays inside its budgets: download (villa.glb + interior.glb + fabrics.ktx2) <= 9 MB (villa3, the owner 2026-11-26: textures streamed with the interior, never at boot); LOD0 <= 62k triangles, LOD1 <= 20k, LOD2 <= 1.5k, one draw per named slot (<= 9 per level); the interior cell <= 230k triangles (villa3) and <= 16 draws (round 2, the furnished rooms), the pool kit node Villa_kit <= 12k triangles / <= 4 draws, drawn only within 70 m (with LOD0) and outside the 9-draw level cap (approved by the owner 2026-11-26), every opaque interior primitive carrying its three baked lights (sky / sun / night: no runtime light, rule fixed-light-count). The drive lane from the gate to the garage's right bay is free of car blockers and no parked car stands in it; the closed gate closes its mouth; the walker finds a floor under every interior spawn, a walkable riser on every stair tread and a floor in the pool. | The owner's first concern for the villa (2026-11-22) was performance: a big detailed house with an interior must not cost the city. A hero with an interior is the case where triangles, draws and a stream-in hitch creep up unseen (the house pilot's first stream-in was a 51-65 ms long task, docs/INTERIOR.md); the first browser test of this villa put a parked SUV in the only bay the player's car could enter (the car stopped against it). | `villa` (tools/audit/villaCheck.mjs) + browser row `villa` (the stream-in hitch, tools/audit/gate.d/browser/villa.mjs) |
| [villa-drive-plane](rules/villa-drive-plane.md) |  (provisional) | A driven paved surface a scripted model adds (the villa's drive and garage floor) is a DESIGNED surface: one plane or one ramp then flat (models/villa/villa.json drive_plane), above the city's terrain everywhere it covers, and the movers use it (a deck in world.decks for the car, a TriBVH with the terrain switched off for the walker, the parked cars on it). | [deck-profile-measured](rules/deck-profile-measured.md) |  (provisional) | An OSM road deck's top follows the bridge's MEASURED profile, not a guess between its ends: every OSM bridge way is either measured (data/overrides.json bridgeProfiles: the UrbIS DSM along its centre line, the carriageway's median every 2 m, outliers off the running median dropped; tools/bridges/deckProfiles.py) or listed with the reason the DSM gives no clean deck surface (the straight line is kept). The first build also showed what a footbridge needs that a road deck does not: the bank covered the stairs cut into it (F4), and carving under a stair right to its end left a 0.16-0.25 m dip where it met the street (F2: the 1 m terrain grid cannot follow a stair's end; the stairs now end in a 1 m pad and the terrain within 1.4 m of a welded end only comes down to the walk). | `footbridge` (tools/audit/footbridgeAudit.mjs: F1 every UrbIS PB over the railway built and its polygon not open over the drop, F2 every end welded to the drawn street / path / platform within 0.15 m, F3 the deck >= 5.2 m over the rails, F4 the bank never over a tread, F5 piers off the tracks, F6 its OSM ways not painted on the ground, F7 real risers / goings; its self-test: --old = ?footbridge=old must FAIL F1) + `bridges` U3 (a PB is carried by a footbridge) |
